finding_key: packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts::`isprivatehost` omits several non-public address ranges (multicast, 240/4 + broadcast, 192.0.0.0/24, 198.18/15) and every ipv6 form that embeds an ipv4 address other than ::ffff:, so 6to4/nat64 spellings of the metadata endpoint pass the guard.
evidence: Verified against isPrivateHost (image-fetcher.ts ~lines 84-109) and unwrapIpv4Mapped (~117). The IPv4 branch only enumerates 0/8,10/8,127/8,169.254/16,172.16-31,192.168/16,100.64/10 and returns false for everything else, so multicast (224/4), broadcast/reserved (240/4, 255.255.255.255), 192.0.0.0/24 and 198.18/15 pass. unwrapIpv4Mapped folds only the ::ffff: prefix, so NAT64 (64:ff9b::a9fe:a9fe) and 6to4 (2002:a9fe:a9fe::) embeddings of 169.254.169.254 return false. assertResolvedHostIsPublic early-returns for anything containing ':' (isIpLiteral), so the resolver half does not catch these literals either — the trace is correct. Real defect, but exploitability of the metadata read is niche (requires a NAT64/6to4 gateway); the common literal/::ffff:/DNS-resolved forms remain covered, so I rate it minor.
